state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you explain why you think Fido falling asleep would result in a negative slope on the graph? Let's think about how distance and time are related in this scenario.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I guess I thought that if Fido was just lying down, he wouldn't be moving away from home, so the line going down meant he was resting. But now I’m not sure if that makes sense. Does the negative slope mean he’s actually moving back towards home instead?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you think of any other scenarios where the distance might decrease even if Fido isn't moving towards home? Let's explore different possibilities that could explain the negative slope on the graph.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively engages the misconception and the student self-corrects to the right interpretation by Turn 2, but Turn 3 inappropriately introduces confusion by suggesting other scenarios when the student has already reached the correct understanding that negative slope means returning home.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently uses probing questions to guide the student's thinking without giving direct answers, though they don't employ counterexamples to expose the flawed reasoning about 'falling asleep,' which would have made it a perfect exemplar.
